summary: Lexy, a young woman in the Enderby household, travels out to meet a train and returns to the city while Mrs. Enderby arranges for Miss Craigie to be sent out for a drive so Lexy can slip away unnoticed. Lexy thinks of Mr. Houseman as her ally, the man she hoped would help her after Caroline's disappearance, since Caroline was to have married him at Wyngate. Returning home in the dark, Lexy finds a letter from Houseman, who waited for her in the park all afternoon and then went to the house, where a servant told him Miss Enderby had gone to the country with her mother. The excerpt ends mid-letter, with Houseman saying he understands and is sorry Caroline did not tell him.
one_line: Lexy, returning from a secret train trip, reads a letter from Mr. Houseman about Caroline's sudden departure and the missed meeting in the park.
key_facts: Miss Craigie is sent out for a drive so that the chauffeur is got rid of while Lexy slips out of the house and down to the station.
Mrs. Enderby's plan goes as she willed it, and Lexy catches the designated train back to the city.
Lexy's great comfort on the journey in is the thought of Mr. Houseman, who she believes will help her.
Mr. Houseman says Caroline promised to meet him last night at a place called Wyngate, where they were to be married.
This morning there was a letter from Caroline postmarked Wyngate, but Houseman says she did not go there.
Lexy reaches the Grand Central after dark and chooses to walk back to the house, at the risk of being late for dinner.
Lexy thinks of Houseman as young like herself, not old and cautious and deliberate, and she trusts him.
The servant Annie tells Lexy that Mrs. Enderby came home in the car half an hour earlier.
A young man left a letter for Lexy about twenty minutes before her return.
The letter is addressed to "Miss Lexy" in a good clear hand.
Houseman writes that he does not know Lexy's other name because he forgot to ask.
Houseman writes that he waited in the park for Lexy all afternoon until it got dark.
Houseman went to the house and asked for Miss Enderby, and a servant told him she had gone away to the country with her mother that morning.
Houseman writes: "Please tell Miss Enderby that I understand. I am sorry she didn't tell me" (the excerpt ends here).
